position: The patch is sound apart from the token refresh path, where a concurrent refresh can hand two callers different tokens. I would land it once F1 is addressed; F2 is worth a follow-up but does not block.

findings.claim: Two concurrent callers of refreshToken() can each start a refresh, so the second write overwrites the first and one caller keeps a token that is already revoked.
findings.fix: Share one in-flight refresh promise per session key and have every caller await it, so the write happens once.

findings.claim: The retry loop logs the full authorization header at debug level, so a debug run writes bearer tokens to disk.
findings.fix: Redact the header value before logging it.

answers.question: Does the change alter the on-disk session format?
answers.answer: No. The stored record keeps the same three fields; only the write path is reordered.

answers.question: Is the added timeout observable by callers?
answers.answer: Yes, as a rejected promise with the existing TimeoutError, so no call site needs to change.

keep_list.claim: Session records stay readable by the previous release.

assumptions: The evidence pack shows the whole refresh path; no other module writes the session record.
